answers.core: It can't, this directly affects the editor code and the GDScript language.
answers.workaround: There are two work-arounds. One is to ignore the problem. Another is to not give your abstract classes `class_name`, but this requires you to use `extends "my_script.gd"` to extend them, and if you want to use the `is` operator then you have to use `const MyScript = preload("my_script.gd")` in every file where you refer to that type.

title: Add support for abstract classes in GDScript
